Jerry Seinfeld turned down $110 MILLION to make one more season of Seinfeld. NBC offered him $5 MILLION per episode, but even the CEO of its parent company couldn't convince him to stay

in 1997, Jerry was already making $1,000,000 per episode, but NBC wanted a tenth season so badly that General Electric CEO Jack Welch personally met with him

During the meeting, Welch pulled Jerry aside, wrote $5,000,000 per episode on a piece of paper, and handed it to him. That's $110 million for another 22 episodes

Afterward, Jerry walked through Central Park with his managers and explained that ending the show was like leaving the stage after a standing ovation. He didn't want to stay so long that people stopped applauding

He rejected the offer, and Seinfeld ended in 1998 after nine seasons!
